version_note: Technique IDs and names follow MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise. ATT&CK is revised periodically (names and tactic assignments can change); verify against the current release before citing in formal reports.

relations.behavior_consistent: The observed log behavior matches the pattern described by the technique. This does not prove an adversary performed it; benign causes (misconfiguration, authorized scanning, user error) are possible.
relations.potential_association: The technique is one plausible explanation for the observed behavior, but the logs alone do not distinguish it from benign activity or other techniques. Treat as a hypothesis.

brute_force.name: Brute Force
brute_force.rationale: Many failed authentication attempts against an account or service in a short period matches the repeated-guessing pattern the technique describes.

password_guessing.name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
password_guessing.rationale: Repeated failures concentrated on one or a few accounts are consistent with guessing passwords for those accounts.

password_spraying.name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
password_spraying.rationale: One source failing authentication once or a few times each across many different accounts is consistent with password spraying.

valid_accounts.name: Valid Accounts
valid_accounts.rationale: A successful login that follows repeated failures, or that is unusual for the account (new network origins, off-hours), could indicate use of valid but compromised credentials. It can equally be a legitimate user who mistyped a password or travelled.

network_service_discovery.name: Network Service Discovery
network_service_discovery.rationale: One source contacting many distinct ports in a short window matches how port scanners enumerate services. Authorized vulnerability scanners and some applications produce the same pattern.

exfiltration_alt_protocol.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exfiltration_alt_protocol.rationale: A large volume of data sent from an internal host to an external address is a prerequisite observation for data exfiltration, but backups, software updates and uploads produce the same signal. Content and intent are not visible in connection logs.

application_layer_protocol.name: Application Layer Protocol
application_layer_protocol.rationale: Internal hosts communicating with an address on a configured watchlist is a possible command-and-control indicator. The watchlist entry itself is only as reliable as its source.

os_credential_dumping_passwd_shadow.name: OS Credential Dumping: /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow
os_credential_dumping_passwd_shadow.rationale: Attempts to read /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd are consistent with credential-file access, but may also be misconfigured jobs or administrators. Only attempts are visible, not successful reads.
